title: Harvest AI - contract uplift and multi-region renegotiation
next_steps: Redwood to send draft 12-month reserved capacity term with EU add-on pricing (Maya)
SE to schedule 30-min latency benchmark session and share benchmark plan (Liam)
Customer to confirm EU data residency requirements and KMS vendor (Elena)
Procurement to circulate redlines and target internal sign-off date (Samir)
action_items: Maya Chen: Draft commercial term with 20% commit discount and EU region pricing — due 2027-01-22
Liam Patel: Prepare benchmark plan (100k token/day test, 99th percentile target, private EU pilot script) — due 2027-01-21
Elena Rossi: Confirm list of regulated datasets for EU pilot + KMS vendor name — due 2027-01-25
Samir Gupta: Share procurement timeline and any required contractual addenda — due 2027-01-26
summary: Check-in to align on Harvest AI's upcoming renewal and planned capacity uplift. Discussed adding EU region (data residency), possible APAC later, reserved capacity pricing, pilot timeline for private deployment, security/compliance questions (SOC2, KMS), and a short benchmark plan. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send draft commercial, SE-run benchmarks, customer to confirm KMS and datasets, procurement to send redlines.
topics: EU region add-on and data residency
Latency and throughput targets; benchmark plan
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call?
[00:04] Elena Rossi: Elena here.
[00:06] Marcus Lee: Marcus, hi.
[00:07] Samir Gupta: Samir.
[00:08] Nina Park: Nina on the line.
[00:10] Liam Patel: Liam from Redwood SE.
[00:12] Maya Chen: Cool, thanks. High level agenda, we want to sync on your renewal window, the proposed uplift, and the EU pilot you mentioned. Also price and security Qs from procurement. Should be about 45 ish minutes?
[00:23] Elena Rossi: Sounds good. We have a tight Q1 sign-off window so appreciate the focus.
[00:27] Samir Gupta: Yep procurement timeline is the end of Jan ideally we want a doc to review.
[00:31] Maya Chen: Perfect. Quick backdrop from our side — you've been on the 2x reserved tier for 6 months, usage spiked after models went into prod, and you flagged needing more headroom plus EU residency for a regulated customer. Is that right Marcus?
[00:47] Marcus Lee: Yeah, usage spiked for inference throughput. Our 95th percentile tail is creeping up during peak hours. Also, European client demands data residency and we prefer a private VPC in eu-west region.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Got it. Liam, do you want to talk about options and what a pilot would look like?
[01:03] Liam Patel: Sure. So there are a couple of levers — reserved capacity bump (we can commit GPUs for you at a discount), add EU region on the Hosted side, or do a Private deploy in your VPC. For the private pilot we usually do a 4-week validation: onboarding, baseline benchmark (latency + throughput + KV cache hit tests), a security checklist run, and then a short canary with real traffic. For EU residency we can provision the private control plane with customer-managed KMS.
[01:29] Elena Rossi: When you say KMS, we need it to integrate with our existing AWS KMS/HSM. Any blockers there?
[01:36] Liam Patel: No on the AWS KMS side, we support AWS KMS and Vault on prem; HSM integrations possible but need an SOW if it's a specialized HSM. We may need some network peering and IAM mapping. Some of the names in the logs can get munged in the transcript, excuse that — but technically it's mapping keys via an encrypted channel.
[01:54] Marcus Lee: Ok, good. For latency targets, our product team wants 95th < 200ms for short prompts and 99th < 600ms for longer chat flows. Can Redwood hit that from eu-west with the private pilot?
[02:07] Liam Patel: Short answer yes, with reserved capacity sized correctly and KV caching enabled. The 99th percent for longer sequences depends on batching and model selection; we recommend a small model shard plus quantization for the EU pilot to reduce token cost. We'll validate in the benchmark.
[02:23] Maya Chen: On pricing we discussed a 20% commit discount in the pre-call notes, but open to structure: a 12-month term with a committed throughput level vs 24-month for deeper discount. Samir, what does procurement prefer?
[02:36] Samir Gupta: We lean toward 12-months but we need to see commercial that lists EU add-on as a line item. If the 24-month moves the price materially, we might discuss. Also need a standard data processing addendum for EU customers.
[02:49] Maya Chen: We can include a data processing addendum and the EU region fee as an explicit line. I'll draft two options (12m/24m) and call out the reserved capacity numbers.
[02:57] Nina Park: One ask on the pilot — can we run a test against a sanitized dataset that mimics PII patterns but isn't real customer data? We want realistic cache behavior.
[03:06] Liam Patel: Absolutely. We do recommend a sanitized corpus so you can simulate KV cache locality and sequence lengths. We'll provide a test harness and scripts.
[03:13] Elena Rossi: About SOC2 compliance — you're SOC2 Type II certified per your docs, but our security team will want to validate logging retention and audit trails. Is that in the standard package or add-on?
[03:24] Liam Patel: SOC2 is standard for the hosted offering. Audit log retention beyond the default retention window can be configured as an add-on. For Private deployments, logs can be forwarded to your SIEM per the deployment playbook.
[03:36] Marcus Lee: And SSO/SAML? We want OKTA-based SSO and role-based access for our ML engineers.
[03:41] Maya Chen: Redwood supports SAML/OKTA and can restrict via RBAC. We'll make sure that's in the operations runbook for the private pilot.
[03:49] Samir Gupta: Legal will want to see the standard indemnity and data clauses. Also, what's your SLA target for dedicated capacity?
[03:56] Liam Patel: For dedicated/reserved capacity we offer SLA-backed uptime with credits — typical latency SLO is in the 99th percentile SSEs but we can surface the exact language in the contract. I'll pull the SLA excerpt into the doc.
[04:07] Maya Chen: For the commercial terms — what we're proposing is: base commit for US-hosted reserved capacity X GPUs, an EU add-on that either uses hosted eu-west with data residency controls or a private pilot in your VPC. 20% discount on the base for a 12-month commit, 25% for 24 months. We'll share a draft.
[04:25] Elena Rossi: Numbers sound fine but we need clarity on burst capacity. In spikes we can't afford throttling.
[04:31] Liam Patel: Burst is configurable — reserved pools can be configured with burst credits or short-term burst capacity. We'll model your traffic and recommend a buffer.
[04:39] Marcus Lee: Can you also share a cost estimate for token-unit vs per-hour GPU so our finance team can evaluate? We have internal run cost metrics.
[04:46] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include both a per-token and per-hour breakdown and an estimated monthly cost at your current usage plus the uplift.
[04:53] Nina Park: SE question — for the private pilot, does Redwood support our internal observability hooks and traces? We need request-level tracing tied to our Tracing system.
[05:02] Liam Patel: We have tracing hooks, Jaeger/OTel support and can push traces to your ingest endpoint. Some field names might be normalized; we'll share the schema.
[05:11] Elena Rossi: Great. Timeline wise, if we want procurement sign-off end of Jan, what's realistic for the pilot window?
[05:18] Maya Chen: If procurement signs end of Jan, we can start the pilot mid-Feb — provisioning + onboarding 1 week, 4-week pilot, then canary and go/no-go in mid-March. Does that align with your roadmap?
[05:29] Elena Rossi: That works. We need the commercial to review by Friday.
[05:33] Samir Gupta: Friday is tight but doable.
[05:35] Maya Chen: Okay I'll push the draft commercial today and final by Friday. Liam will follow up with the benchmark plan.
[05:40] Liam Patel: I'll include the benchmark script, expected metrics (95/99 latency, throughput, cache hit rate), and infra checklist.
[05:46] Marcus Lee: One more thing — can we get an architecture diagram for the private pilot with network requirements?
[05:51] Liam Patel: Yes diagram and peering steps; I'll attach the VPC peering and IAM mapping steps.
[05:57] Maya Chen: Cool. Any other questions?
[06:00] Nina Park: No, that's all.
[06:02] Elena Rossi: Thanks everyone.
[06:04] Maya Chen: Thanks — recap: Redwood sends commercial (Maya), SE shares benchmark and architecture (Liam), customer confirms EU datasets/KMS (Elena), procurement sends redlines (Samir). We'll reconvene after procurement cycles.
[06:16] Samir Gupta: Thanks.
[06:17] Liam Patel: Thanks all.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Bye.
